question: Is the matched confirmation advantage reproducible under independently initialized learned tensors and a different training sample order?
protocol: Use identically ordered tokenized user turns, native unrestricted greedy first-turn decoding, identical generation limits, common-prefix animal probes and end-to-end timings. The two variants use the same pretrained decoder and native layers 10..15 for recurrent evidence. An equal-training fit repeats the original seed, parameters, optimizer, steps, all training targets including both support labels, and all 240 stories. No selection or fitting on test. All fixed-weight arms are bound by digest. Preserve all hyperparameters and all input IDs, support targets, generated-answer labels and scorer from the successful paired test. The span-only conditions retain both learned evidence reads and the complete full-vocabulary decoder; they feed the first-pass sentence states to the second read in place of re-entering layers 10..15. All other operations remain identical. Compare actual cost and common-prefix probes.
gate: Evidence for superiority in this diagnostic requires eight net additional correct responses, paired exact p<.05, four net probes and at most 1.5x control time. A tie leaves incremental superiority over this comparison unestablished. Do not use the diagnostic to tune this checkpoint.
